summary: Opened a new sourced lead rather than extending the parent's variant list. The drift the parent now documents raises the recorded accepted indexes that OmniPaxos itself trusts in two places, and one of them is the trim bound: SequencePaxos::trim derives its bound from the minimum of the leader's recorded accepted indexes (with no explicit index it uses that minimum and otherwise compares the request against it, reporting the same minimum in the error), while the documented contract for trimming requires that ALL nodes have decided the trim index; the newly registered child question asks whether a drifted minimum can therefore let trim remove entries a replica has not decided, or push the compacted index past the entries a replica still holds, with a later re-synchronization of that replica then asking its storage for a suffix below the compacted index (MemoryStorage computes that by subtracting the compacted index, so an over-compaction would underflow). Updates: four sources record the trim derivation, the minimum helper, the documented requirement and MemoryStorage's trim/suffix arithmetic; a behaviour records that trim's bound comes from recorded accepted indexes rather than any decided index per node; and the child interpretation is source-only with conclusion and defect_claim unresolved, including the honest counter-arguments that keep it unsettled (in the observed drift the leading node's own recorded value stayed at its content so the minimum remained truthful, and try_trim's StopSign adjustment cancelled the observed drift exactly) and the limits (trim after a drift was not exercised, no observed state had every recorded value above its content at a trim, and the underflow hypothesis rests on reading MemoryStorage). The parent question's discriminator now also names this consumer alongside the bound and reconfiguration-handoff questions. No execution was requested this turn; incomplete are the trim-after-drift probe, the drift's bound and handoff questions, timers and loss triggers, larger clusters, and persistence.
